signature_moves: Per-participant identity color as a full presence system — one pastel hue binds each collaborator's name pill, live cursor, and freehand annotations into a pre-attentively locatable identity (find who-is-where by color, confirm by label)
Softening the collaborator hues to pastel tints (not saturated) is what makes a pro remote-control tool feel human
Freehand annotation over the live screen as the foregrounded default tool — pointing at code by drawing on it, not by moving a shared cursor
defects: Contrast Dilution (low confidence, marketing render) — same-hue tinted name pills pair a pale fill with a saturated same-hue label; rust-on-peach and blue-on-pale-blue plausibly under 4.5:1. Mitigated: label+cursor co-present, color never the sole signal. Verify against real in-app colors before treating as canon.

aesthetic.direction: friendly / humanist neo-grotesque product — heavy bold grotesque display + violet-indigo brand + a pastel multi-hue presence palette, warming the Linear/Vercel dev-tool register rather than going dark-and-electric

psychology: Von Restorff effect — each participant's distinct hue makes their presence the one different thing, so who-is-where is located pre-attentively before any name is read
Social facilitation / co-presence — visible name pills + live cursors surface collaborators, converting cold remote control into felt togetherness
Jakob's Law — annotation tools (arrow, hand, pen, draw) reuse familiar drawing-app conventions so users transfer expectations with no learning cost
Aesthetic-usability effect — pastel, rounded, hand-drawn treatment lowers the intimidation of a screen-control power tool

Signal detection / mode indication — the single highlighted active tool breaks the monochrome toolbar pattern, keeping the current annotation mode findable (predictability, the right lever for an expert tool, not option-reduction)
notes: PRIMARY CAVEAT: input is a single 1200x630 OG marketing composite, not a raw window capture. Left half = brand only (wordmark/logo/headline). Right half = a stylized mock of the GUEST's shared macOS screen (wallpaper + Apple menu bar + a PaidUsersList.tsx code editor) — that is NOT Tuple's UI; only the overlay layer (annotation toolbar, name pills, cursors, freehand ink) plus the wordmark are Tuple design evidence. App rendered at unknown scale => NO point-accurate control sizing derivable; all UI-size tokens are estimated/omitted. Outer-frame traffic lights are flat-grey illustration, not genuine chrome. Lineage recorded native (Tuple is a known AppKit-native app) but confidence LOW from this image alone. No glass evidence either way => insufficient-evidence for era. Most rubric/native checks are n/a because the genuine surface is a HUD, not a full window.
